prize_parts.citation: for the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson with the ATLAS and CMS experiments

statement.case_for: The 2013 prize honoured the theory of the mass mechanism, but the particle itself, found by two independent experiments in 2012, is the decisive clue from nature that completed the Standard Model. A discovery of this size, confirmed independently and followed by a decade of coupling and spin-parity measurements, is the clearest example on our shortlist of nature answering a question the theory had posed for half a century. The instrument and analysis achievements behind it are of the kind the committee has repeatedly rewarded, and recognition is overdue rather than early. Nothing else on the list combines such large empirical consequence with such complete maturity. Having heard the colleagues, I keep it first, but I hold it with less confidence than in my opening ballot because the attribution problem is real.
statement.case_against: Its weak point is attribution. Thousands of people built and analysed the two experiments, and naming the founding spokespersons (Jenni for ATLAS, Della Negra and Virdee for CMS) is a defensible proxy, not an obvious finding of who made the decisive contribution. Only two of eight members ranked it at all, and the one other ballot, from Eva Lindroth, placed it eighth and said plainly that it is awkward to credit individuals in huge collaborations. Another reservation is that the committee has long avoided collaboration discoveries and might see this as the experimental half of a prize already given in 2013. If the expert reports cannot support these three names, the strongest alternatives are B036 and B025, where attribution is cleaner.

responses.point: She ranked the Higgs discovery eighth. She grants its importance but finds crediting a few individuals in collaborations of thousands awkward, and she defers on particle physics.
responses.response: The concern is fair and it is my own largest reservation, so I do not dismiss it. I would answer that the Nobel statutes have always forced a choice of at most three, and the experiments were conceived and led by identifiable people over two decades, which is a different situation from a diffuse effort with no leadership. The question is whether the reports can show those three are the right proxies. I would not defend the names against evidence to the contrary, and if that evidence fails I would move to B025 or B036. I still disagree that awkward attribution justifies ranking the most consequential discovery of the period last in the shortlist.

responses.point: He ranks optical lattice clocks (B025) first, as a new measurement capability at the 1e-18 level that opens geodesy, constants tests and a redefinition of the second, with a clean two-person credit.
responses.response: I agree that the attribution is much cleaner than in my case, and the maturity is real. Where I differ is on the word discovery. The clock is a superb instrument, but the physics it has so far delivered is bounds and capability, not a new fact about the world. The decisive test for me is what nature has told us, and so far the clocks have confirmed that nothing is wrong. I would also want to hear how much of the result is Jun Ye's building on the comb work already rewarded in 2005. I treat B025 as a strong alternative, not a lesser one, and I could support it if the committee prefers clean attribution to scale.

responses.point: He ranks topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect (B036) first, for the Kane-Mele theory and the HgTe measurement of quantized edge conductance, and he sees some unresolved credit for Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang.
responses.response: This is the case where theory was tied most quickly to measurement, which I rank highly, and I put it fifth in my own list. My qualification is the 2016 prize for topological phases, which Mehlig and Johansson also raise. Haldane and Thouless gave the concept of topological order in condensed matter, and the committee must ask whether this is a distinct discovery or the next chapter. I do not think it is only a chapter, because Z2 invariants and protected boundary states of time-reversal-symmetric systems were a real conceptual advance. The credit dispute is more serious. Excluding Bernevig and Hughes, who predicted the HgTe effect, and Zhang's death in 2018, leave an incomplete record. I would hold B036 as the principal alternative if the reports settle that.

responses.point: He ranks IceCube (B007) first for opening neutrino astronomy with a cubic-kilometre ice detector, backed by the diffuse flux, the TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic-plane signal.
responses.response: We agree on the importance, and I ranked it fourth. My difference is timing. The diffuse flux is established, but the sources of most of it are unidentified, and I am wary of rewarding an instrument before the first physics story is done. A candidate with one blazar and a Galactic signal is not yet Higgs-like in maturity, and Baikal and AMANDA pioneers further complicate the two names. I would not stand in the way of a prize here, but I think it is a few years early and would rather wait for the source population.

responses.point: He ranks the KPZ universality class (B017) first and proposes crediting Kardar and Zhang, with Parisi's 2021 prize leaving a difficulty, and he sees Takeuchi's experiments as optional.
responses.response: I respect the elegance and the exact solutions in one dimension, but I did not rank it, and I would be uneasy about a theory-first prize for a model whose experimental confirmation is partial in some systems, as he himself notes. I would also be wary of dropping Parisi from a paper on which he is a co-author, since a prize that names two of three authors invites the obvious question. The case would be stronger if Takeuchi's liquid-crystal results were decisive, but then the credited trio is not the trio he proposes.

uncertainties: Whether the founding spokespersons of ATLAS and CMS are the right three names, and whether the expert reports can support them.
Whether the committee will accept a collaboration-based experimental discovery after the 2013 theory prize.
Whether optical lattice clocks should be judged as a measurement discovery or an enabling technology, which determines how strongly B025 competes.
Whether topological insulators are distinct enough from the 2016 prize to count as a separate achievement.
statement.conflict_note: I am the committee's Secretary and a string theorist with no personal link to any shortlisted candidate. David Gross, my PhD supervisor, is not on the shortlist. No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile.
